items.definition: The right to vote. Watch who has it and who does not — the answer changes in almost every unit.
hints: It's about a specific right tied to elections.
Whether or not someone is allowed to cast a ballot.

items.definition: Government in which the people hold power, directly or through representatives they elect.
hints: Think about where the power sits — with the people, directly or indirectly.
It's the broader category; a republic is one specific type of it.

items.definition: A government where citizens elect representatives to decide for them. The Founders chose a republic, not a direct democracy — and said so.
hints: This is the specific kind of democracy the Founders actually chose.
Citizens don't vote on every law themselves — they elect people to do it for them.

items.definition: Full membership in a nation, with its rights and duties. Who counts as a citizen is one of this course's longest arguments.
hints: Think about membership, not just residency.
It comes with both rights and duties, and who qualifies for it changes over time in this course.

items.definition: The idea that colonies exist to enrich the mother country — supplying raw materials, buying finished goods.
hints: This is about the economic purpose colonies were expected to serve.
Raw materials go one way, finished goods come back — who's meant to profit most?

items.definition: Britain's long stretch of loosely enforcing colonial trade laws. When enforcement returned after 1763, colonists experienced it as a change, not as normal.
hints: This is about enforcement — or the lack of it.
Britain wasn't strictly enforcing its own trade laws for a long stretch, until 1763.

items.definition: Virginia's elected assembly, 1619 — the first representative body in the English colonies.
hints: It's the first elected representative body in the English colonies.

items.definition: 1620 agreement by Plymouth colonists to govern themselves by majority rule. An early case of consent of the governed.
hints: Plymouth colonists agreeing, before they even landed, to govern themselves by majority rule.

_hint_model: 2 escalating hints per item, available during the regular season only. Playoffs run cold (no hints), per BK's ruling 2026-09-22.
